questions.prompt: Why is uniform circular motion described as accelerated motion?
options: The direction of motion keeps changing
questions.explain: A change in direction is a change in velocity.

questions.prompt: A merry-go-round seat moves in a circle of radius 7 m and completes one lap in 22 s. What is its speed (use π = 22/7)?
In uniform circular motion, what is the direction of the velocity at any point?
options: Along the tangent to the circle
questions.explain: Velocity is always along the direction of motion.

questions.prompt: A stone whirled on a string is released. Which way does it fly?
options: Along the tangent at the point of release
questions.explain: No force now changes its direction.

questions.prompt: Earth orbits the Sun at about 1.5 × 10⁸ km in 365 days. Roughly what is its orbital speed in km/s? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
What provides the inward force that lets a car turn around a bend on a flat road?
options: Friction between the tyres and the road
questions.explain: That is why turning on wet or oily roads is dangerous.

questions.prompt: If the radius of the circle is doubled but the time per lap stays the same, by what factor does the speed increase?
questions.explain: v = 2πr ÷ T: doubling r doubles v.

questions.prompt: A satellite moves in a circular orbit at constant speed. Which statement is true?
options: Its speed is constant but its velocity keeps changing
Both speed and velocity are constant
